title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
What does it take to make Just Transitions Scenarios a reality?
To begin to answer this, we studied how each scenario would be governed.





What is governance?






What is governance? Governance is the collection of, “actors, rules, and processes through which decisions are made and implemented.”4








Read more






Governance is not limited to the activities of government agencies, and the complete picture is much more complex than we can fully predict. For our preliminary analysis, we didn’t consider completely new:

laws and policies
institutions
sources of funding

Instead, for each scenario we focused on the different levels of importance of existing organizations in the Delta, and existing proposed actions to manage the Delta. Ultimately, this roughly sketches out:

Who are the key players?
How might they carry out the scenario?

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Scenarios by Strategy Area
In this chart, each scenario is shown with its overall alignment with Adaptation Plan actions, grouped by the four strategy areas. The total score of each bar comprises a mix of both numbers of actions and strength of alignment. In other words, the larger the bar, the greater the number of weighted adaptive actions.






Read more






In interpreting this graph, it is important to remember that this primarily covers actions that provide resilience for salinity management in the Delta as it undergoes climate change, and the list of actions are non-exhaustive. Additionally, some caution should be exercised in its interpretation because we do not know the level of impact any one action might provide. Nor can we say with certainty which actions are linchpins for any scenario. Our findings are only preliminary.

Top Actions Overall
Across all scenarios, these are identified as the top actions.7 More important actions may be identified as the larger cells on the right. 






The purpose of this chart is to facilitate exploring the actions on your own time, not to demonstrate the relative importance of any strategy area.

There are more actions addressing the ecosystem due to the greater number of actions in New Green Watershed compared to other scenarios. New Green Watershed has the largest number of votes, and the Tunnel had the least.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Eco Machine
There are 52 actions aligned with Eco Machine.






For the following slides, please pay attention to the changing scale for “score”.










Read more






The most important actions for this scenario derive from interventions in the ecosystem. Flood risk mitigation actions may also support Eco Machine (EM) priorities, but most of these appear as a third tier of interventions that are not directly performed in EM. This means that while a lot of flood risk mitigation actions might support EM, they are not integral to making this scenario possible. In addition, many ecosystem interventions also appear as supportive. Among the four main strategy areas, Water Supply Reliability and Agriculture had few directly pertinent interventions related to EM.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
New Green Watershed
There are 77 actions aligned with New Green Watershed.






Read more






NGW has the most AP actions. Most of the top ranked actions for NGW prioritize ecosystem interventions, but also agriculture and flood risk reduction also play important roles in setting up this scenario for success.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Tunnel
There are 8 actions aligned with Tunnel. The Tunnel has the least potential number of actions and lowest alignment with the AP. No adaptive action directly targets the building blocks for this scenario. Finally, no core actions were identified as “unique” to Tunnel.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Bolster & Fortify
There are 25 actions aligned with Bolster & Fortify. Only three AP actions are directly performed under Bolster & Fortify, and these all directly relate to the infrastructure necessary to realize the scenario.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Calling on Reserves
There are 24 actions aligned with Calling on Reserves. Unsurprisingly, the key strategy areas for Calling on Reserves involve flood risk reduction and water supply reliability. This scenario has one adaptive action that would be directly implemented and one that is “partly performed”. The former concerns reservoir storage capacities and the latter concerns “functional flows” which ties the needs of the ecosystem to how much water is released from reservoirs.

title: Just Transitions Governance - DRAFT
text:
Increased Flows
There are 37 actions aligned with 30% Increased Tiered Outflow. Similar to Tunnel, no adaptation actions were identified would be directly performed under this scenario. Finally, no core actions were identified as unique to 30% Increased Tiered Outflow.

Lead Actor Types
Here we see how the lead actors are grouped by their type of organization. One takeaway is that the state is most important, but regional and local governments matter too.
